report.incident_title: Intermittent checkout failures, but dashboards are all green
report.summary: The checkout failures are real and platform-side, not user-side. Checkout-svc error rate stepped from about 0.3% to 1.1-1.3% at about 10:20Z on 2026-07-09 and stayed there through 11:25Z, which the ~1% dashboard figure hides behind a normal average. Confirmed by tool results: checkout WARN logs at 10:22:10, 10:31:44 and 10:52:19Z report inventory reserve timeouts after 3000ms; inventory-svc p99 on node ip-10-0-3-17 rose from about 420ms to about 4.6-4.7s from 10:20Z; one trace (t-c05-slow-1) shows a 3820ms rocksdb.get on pod inventory-svc-5d8-m4c on that node, which exceeded checkout's 3000ms timeout; a comparison trace on node ip-10-0-1-22 completed in 3ms. No alerts fired and readiness stayed at 100%, so the degradation went undetected by alerting. No deploys, config changes or infra events were recorded. Assumptions, not observed: that pods inventory-svc-5d8-xk2 and -p9t run on ip-10-0-3-17 (no node attribution was obtained for them), that ip-10-0-3-17 is in eu-west-1c, and that the cause of the RocksDB slowness is local disk or EBS I/O (no node-level resource metrics were available). The evidence rests on two traces and three log lines, and no metrics or traces were returned before 10:00Z on 2026-07-09.
report.root_cause: Probable mechanism at medium confidence: RocksDB reads in inventory-svc pods on node ip-10-0-3-17 (confirmed for pod inventory-svc-5d8-m4c) became very slow from about 10:20Z, with rocksdb.get taking about 3.8s and node p99 about 4.6s. Those reads exceeded checkout-svc's 3000ms timeout on reserveInventory, so checkout returned AVAILABILITY_UNCONFIRMED. Only the requests routed to the affected pods fail, which is why the aggregate error rate is about 1% and average latency stays flat. The underlying trigger of the RocksDB slowness on that node is not established; no node resource metrics or infra events confirm a node-level fault.

hypotheses.statement: High RocksDB read latency on node ip-10-0-3-17 caused inventory-svc p99 latency spikes (~4–4.7s) that exceeded checkout-svc’s 3000ms timeout, leading to intermittent “availability_unconfirmed” errors.

facts.text: Trace t-c05-slow-1 (2026-07-09T10:40:00Z) has status error and duration 3010ms, with checkout-svc reserveInventory error 'timeout'. The inventory-svc rocksdb.get span took 3820ms on pod inventory-svc-5d8-m4c, node ip-10-0-3-17. The inventory span is longer than the checkout timeout, so the storage read itself was slow.

Trace t-c05-ok-1 (2026-07-09T10:40:05Z) is status ok, 160ms end-to-end. Its inventory-svc rocksdb.get took 3ms on pod inventory-svc-5d8-r7w, node ip-10-0-1-22. The same 10:40 window shows a fast path on another node and a slow path on ip-10-0-3-17, which fits node-specific slowness.

inventory-svc latency_p99 for node=ip-10-0-3-17 rose from ~420ms (10:00-10:10) to 900ms at 10:15 and ~4,600-4,720ms from 10:20 through 11:25, persisting through the end of the window. Other nodes/AZs (eu-west-1a ~410ms, 1b ~405ms) stayed flat; eu-west-1c p99 also jumped to ~3.9-4.1s from 10:20, which is consistent with ip-10-0-3-17 being located in 1c (AZ-to-node mapping not confirmed by tools).

Trace t-c05-slow-1 (2026-07-09T10:40:00Z): checkout-svc reserveInventory took 3010ms with status error, attr error=timeout; the child inventory-svc rocksdb.get span took 3820ms on pod inventory-svc-5d8-m4c, node ip-10-0-3-17. Trace t-c05-ok-1 at 10:40:05Z succeeded in 160ms with rocksdb.get 3ms on pod inventory-svc-5d8-r7w, node ip-10-0-1-22. Only 2 traces returned, so sample is very small.

Re-check of inventory-svc latency_p99 for node=ip-10-0-3-17 over 10:00-11:30Z: ~420ms at 10:00-10:10, 900ms at 10:15, then 4600-4720ms from 10:20 through 11:25 (5-minute points, returned range ends 11:25Z). Series has no per-pod breakdown; available labels are az and node only.

Pod-to-node mapping for inventory-svc pods could only be confirmed for one pod. Trace t-c05-slow-1 (2026-07-09T10:40:00Z) shows the inventory-svc rocksdb.get span on pod inventory-svc-5d8-m4c running on node ip-10-0-3-17 (3820ms). Pods 5d8-xk2 and 5d8-p9t have no node attribution in any tool result, so they cannot be confirmed on ip-10-0-3-17.

assumptions: The observed RocksDB get span on inventory-svc-5d8-m4c is representative of persistent storage latency issues on that node across the incident window.
Node-level p99 metrics accurately reflect the storage latency experienced by all pods on ip-10-0-3-17.

corrective_actions.action: Cordon and drain node ip-10-0-3-17, or otherwise remove inventory-svc pods on that node from the checkout path, so reads are served by healthy nodes; then confirm checkout error rate returns to about 0.3%.
corrective_actions.rationale: Trace and node p99 data tie the slow reads to that node, and draining it is the fastest way to stop failures for affected shoppers. The pod-to-node mapping for pods xk2 and p9t must be checked first, because the claim that they are on this node is unverified.

corrective_actions.action: Investigate the node's storage path (EBS volume latency, iowait, disk saturation, RocksDB compaction or cache state) and replace the node if the fault is local; then re-warm the local RocksDB stock cache on the replacement.
corrective_actions.rationale: The RocksDB read is the slow step, and no node-level metrics have been checked yet, so the trigger is still unknown. Replacing the node is the likely fix if the fault is local to the instance.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts on inventory-svc latency_p99 per node and per AZ, and on checkout error rate over a short window, so the step at 10:20Z would have fired an alert.
corrective_actions.rationale: No alert fired for a sustained 4.6s p99 and a rise of about 1 percentage point in error rate, so the alerting path missed this incident.

corrective_actions.action: Make the inventory-svc readiness or health check reflect RocksDB read latency, or add a per-node slow-read signal, so a degraded node is taken out of rotation instead of passing /ping.
corrective_actions.rationale: Readiness stayed at 100% while the pods on ip-10-0-3-17 were returning reads slower than checkout's timeout.

corrective_actions.action: Once the trigger is found, add node-level storage health monitoring and a runbook for inventory-svc slow-read degradation. Also confirm pod placement and per-pod metrics so that per-pod failure shares can be measured.
corrective_actions.rationale: Pod placement and per-pod metrics are not available from the current tools, and the runbook source returned nothing, so future responders have no guidance.
